summary: Pre-season update: the 7 team bikes were built by Trek and picked up for first test rides, the route was finalized, and the crowdfunding goal was still $50k. Learning-festival workshops (motors, electricity, 3D modeling, chemical reactions) were being prepped.
learning_festival: Prep for upcoming LFs; planned topics: motors, electricity, 3D modeling, chemical reactions. No venue given.
contacts: Trek crew - built all 7 team bikes
Joseph and Sarah (2025 team) - Husky Mind Podcast interview about the team
planning_notes: Trek built all 7 bikes before the season; pick up and test-ride bikes early so any build issues surface before departure.
Crowdfunding goal was $50k on crowdfund.mit.edu as of Feb 2026.

summary: Packing day in the Boston area: the team fit bikes, camping gear, and LF supplies into a rented cargo van and a minivan, and spent hours rigging the roof storage bag, which needed a different strap setup than the 2025 method. They slept around 3 AM before a 6 AM departure for DC.
learning_festival: No event; LF supplies packed into two large bins for the first festival.
contacts: Spokes 2025 team (Sarah) - advised by phone on roof storage
Noah (Tatiana's boyfriend) and Sandeep (Aarushi's dad) - helped rig roof storage
planning_notes: The 2026 minivan has no roof rails, so the 2025 roof-storage method did not work. Test-fit the soft top bag at home first; the fix was running the straps to the rear window.
Cargo van (bikes) and minivan (people and gear) left together; plan packing to finish the day before if possible, since packing ran all day.
Packing that fit: LF supplies in 2 bins, kitchen in 1, bike gear and first aid in 1.

summary: Drove from Boston to DC in the minivan and cargo van. Roof straps slammed the windows and the dashboard alarmed on the unbuckled middle seat until they fixed it. They arrived around 7:30 PM and spent the night precutting felt, cardboard and paper for the next day's festival.
slept_at: Deepika and Nikunj's home, DC (family friends of Aarushi; three rooms with mattresses)
learning_festival: Prep lock-in for the first DC festival at the DC Department of Corrections Youth Services Center, about 120 students expected. The facility bans scissors and sharp objects, so all materials were precut.
contacts: Deepika and Nikunj (Aarushi's family friends), DC - hosted, dinner
planning_notes: DC Youth Services Center bans scissors, glass and sharp objects: precut all felt, cardboard and paper before entering.
Minivan dashboard alarm sounds when heavy bags sit on an unbuckled middle seat; buckle it and check roof straps at the first gas stop.

summary: First learning festival at the DC Youth Services Center, a juvenile rehab facility. The team ran seven rotations of the Lego electric-motor workshop; only some students got motors working, though one class of boys all did.
slept_at: Host's house in DC (Deepika and Nikunj's, per the Day 2 post)
learning_festival: DC Youth Services Center: Lego electric-motor build, seven rotations; the judge's law interns helped run stations.
contacts: Judge Zia Fariqui, DC - created the opportunity and lent his law interns to help run festivals
planning_notes: Lego motor builds are tricky: expect only a minority of students to get a working motor. The facility science teacher's advice was that small wins are the goal.
Ask the host facility for staff or interns to help run stations; the judge's interns covered for the team.
Costco in DC requires the card owner to be present at checkout; the team's borrowed-card workaround did not work reliably.

summary: Rode 88.6 miles from DC to Linden VA after a late, sleep-deprived start. Nate missed a turn and rode a four-lane highway with no shoulder before SAGging about 6 miles; Aarushi, Nunu and Caroline were SAG'd at mile 76.
slept_at: Warmshowers host Jen and Jim's home, Linden VA
contacts: Jen and Jim, Warmshowers hosts in Linden VA - hosted; Jim SAG'd three riders; Jen has hosted MIT Spokes four times
Nikunj and Deepika (Aarushi's uncle and aunt), DC - hosted and shuttled the team to the DC start
planning_notes: Leaving DC at rush hour: the team left at 8:40 AM and reached the Lincoln Memorial at 10 AM. Leave earlier to avoid peak traffic.
The W&OD trail out of DC is separated, shaded and green, with good riding to about mile 40.

A right turn out of a rest-stop parking lot (about mile 55) sent a rider onto a parallel road with a 1000 ft climb and a four-lane 60 mph highway with no bike shoulder. Check shoulders on Street View before accepting a reroute.

Jen warned that the next day's planned 60-mile, ~8000 ft route had sharp, low-visibility turns; the team swapped to a 30-mile, 2000 ft route to a different campground. Ask local hosts about the next day before finalizing.
A SAG pickup spot had a 'No trespassers. Violators will be shot' sign; choose a different pickup point if one looks unsafe.
Riding 88 miles after days of 2-4 hours of sleep caused most of the team to SAG. Consider a shorter opening ride.

summary: Short 31.8-mile ride from Linden to Luray VA. A stranger, Jimmy Baker, donated $1,000 at a gas-pump rest stop, and a pizza place donated pizzas after a phone call. The team stayed at a campground with a pool.
slept_at: Campground near Luray VA (pool, clean bathrooms, jumping pad, volleyball and a pool table; name not given)
contacts: Jimmy Baker - donated $1,000 at a rest stop in Virginia and offered to buy food later
Pizza place in the town near the Luray campground - donated pizzas for dinner (name not given)
Tim, Jen's husband (Linden VA) - drove the team down the gravel mountain
planning_notes: The campground near Luray has a pool, clean bathrooms, jumping pad, volleyball and a pool table; a strong recovery stop.
Calling a town's pizza place ahead of arrival got meals donated near Luray VA.
The gas-pump rest stop near Luray had no shade or overhang; plan shaded lunch spots.

summary: Rode 62.5 miles from Luray to Waynesboro VA along the Shenandoah. Tents, bike shoes and laundry left out overnight were soaked with dew, and the team stopped at a picnic oasis for a long lunch. Host Pam picked them up over the mountain to her Shannon Farm home.
slept_at: Pam's home on Shannon Farm (intentional community), VA
contacts: Pam, Shannon Farm near Waynesboro VA - picked the team up over the mountain and hosted a barbecue dinner
planning_notes: Gear left out overnight was soaked with dew by morning, even without rain in the forecast. Pack wet gear into dry bags and keep bike shoes and laundry indoors.
Waynesboro was a route break: the host picked up the team over the mountain and the team resumed riding from Waynesboro the next day.

summary: Rest day at Pam's Shannon Farm: the team slept in, played card games, floated on the community lake on a 7-person floatie, and attended Pam's potluck. A spider was found in one cabin's bed.
slept_at: Pam's home, Shannon Farm, VA
contacts: Pam - hosted the team and their potluck
JMU students at the Shannon lake - lent a paddle and shared community history
planning_notes: Bring a backup pump: the floatie's pump failed and riders inflated it by mouth.
Shannon Farm's home had no Wi-Fi; the community center did, which is where the team worked on blogs and bookings.
Ticks and mosquitoes at the outdoor picnic; bring bug spray.

summary: Learning festival at the Fluvanna County Public Library with about 70 kids: chemistry for middle and high schoolers, felt-monster genetics for kindergarteners. Afterward two riders waited 30 minutes at a community center a mile away until someone drove them back.
slept_at: Pam's home, Shannon Farm, VA
learning_festival: Fluvanna County Public Library: about 70 kids; middle/high chemistry experiment; kindergarten felt-monster genetics; post-LF ice cream. The library is a family summer hotspot and is supported by the Friends of Fluvanna nonprofit.
contacts: Fluvanna County Public Library staff - hosted the festival; Friends of Fluvanna nonprofit raises money for the library
planning_notes: Fluvanna County Public Library is a good LF partner with a busy family crowd, supported by the Friends of Fluvanna nonprofit.
Kindergarteners need help cutting and gluing felt-monster eyes; encouragement was what they needed most.
Camping gear packed wet on Day 4 grew mildew and was infested with spiders and very large ants. Air tents and pads outdoors and inspect before packing.
Wegman's has a deli and a sushi counter and is a good one-stop grocery for a few days of food.
The community center about a mile from the host house had no transport at night; arrange a pickup in advance.

summary: Rode 41.9 miles from Waynesboro to Lexington VA after a borrowed-truck shuttle to the route start. Two riders spent over an hour at urgent care and a CVS pharmacy waiting on a prescription signature. Host Dirk took the team to the river that evening.
slept_at: Dirk's home, Lexington VA (host)
contacts: Dirk and his wife (Krissie per the Day 9 post) - hosted; river paddleboarding and an off-road sunset drive; dinner
planning_notes: Waynesboro urgent care: a 1+ hour wait, and the prescription was not sent to the CVS pharmacy until a signature was obtained. Call ahead to confirm the prescription is sent.
The Waynesboro CVS restroom was locked and the staff member had no key; ask for a restroom key up front on a long route.
A truck stop between Waynesboro and Lexington has Popeyes, Papa John's and Subway, a good lunch stop on this route.
Tatiana's derailleur was missing gears; a rider fixed it at the midway point. Carry basic derailleur tools.

summary: Rode 67.5 miles from Lexington to Roanoke VA. A rider's chain kept falling off, and the team spent a 3-hour evening meeting working out how ride pace and priorities should fit together.
slept_at: Steve and Debbie's home, Roanoke VA (hosts)
contacts: Steve and Debbie - Roanoke hosts; cooked dinner
planning_notes: A chain that keeps falling off usually means a misaligned derailleur; the team fixed it at the side of the road and again at night. Carry derailleur tools and know how to align one.
Agree on ride pace and priorities before the day: a 3-hour evening team meeting was needed to resolve it.

summary: Rode 40.5 miles from Roanoke to Blacksburg VA, plus a hike up McAfee Knob. Host Steve rode the first 20 miles, and the final 750 ft climb in 3 miles led to host Ann's house.
slept_at: Ann's home, Blacksburg VA (host)
contacts: Steve (Roanoke VA) - host; rode the first 20 miles with the team
Ann (Blacksburg VA) - host; did her own cross-Illinois trip at age 14
Dirk and Krissie - donated eggs for breakfast
planning_notes: McAfee Knob trail: 4 miles each way from the trailhead. With the hike, the day was about 48.5 miles and 4,794 ft.
The final approach to Ann's house in Blacksburg is 750 ft of climbing in 3 miles.
Cyclist hosts like Steve may ride part of the route with the team and know local roads.

summary: Rode 83 miles from Blacksburg to Tazewell VA. Aarushi hit a pothole and crashed into a tree; Hokie Spokes in Blacksburg fully repaired her bike the same day. Riders sheltered from a storm at a Narrows church, and Nunu was SAG'd at mile 65 for knee pain.
slept_at: Tazewell United Methodist Church house (host Teresa)
contacts: Hokie Spokes bike shop, Blacksburg VA - fully repaired Aarushi's bike the same day
Trek shop, Blacksburg VA - warranty replacement helmet and repaired handlebars; no barrel adjuster part for a week
Teresa, Tazewell United Methodist Church - host; stocked the fridge
Bruce ($41) and Wendy ($20) - donations in Blacksburg after overhearing the Spokes story
planning_notes: Hokie Spokes bike shop sits next to a Blacksburg coffee shop and did a same-day repair; the Trek shop could not get a part for a week.
The 1-year helmet warranty covered a replacement helmet after the crash.
Minivan with 3 people plus 3 bikes was possible after rearranging the rack.
Dairy Queen about 30 miles into this route is a good ice-cream stop.
Storm sheltering: riders sat on church steps and napped on concrete for about 2 hours. Plan shelter early when storms are on radar.
Cycle Life PT (Brendan) advised that sharp, repetitive pain means stop riding; the team used this rule to SAG Nunu at mile 65.

summary: Small-town learning festival at the Tazewell United Methodist Church: iodine color-change chemistry for older kids and felt-monster genetics for little kids. Afterward Aarushi and Tatiana joined the church women's group, and Aarushi started a playlist of songs from people they met.
slept_at: Tazewell church house (host Teresa)
learning_festival: Tazewell United Methodist Church: iodine color-change reaction for older kids and felt-monster genetics for little kids. Kids were very engaged; the festival was a small-town highlight.
contacts: Teresa, Tazewell United Methodist Church - host with the warmest heart
Tazewell church women's group - welcomed the team to their gathering
planning_notes: Keeping a list of favorite songs with each stranger's name and town made a good record of people met along the route; it is easy to lose track otherwise.
A small-town church LF has a strong effect on kids and can be low-cost to run.

summary: Rode 72.6 miles from Tazewell to Breaks Interstate Park VA, climbing Big A Mountain. The route passed a no-trespassing gate after a last-minute change, plus several dogs. Dinner was free in Elkhorn City KY, and the team camped at the park.
slept_at: Breaks Interstate Park campground, VA (no electricity or water, per Day 13)
contacts: Taylor, owner of Mi Rancho Mexican Bar and Grill, Elkhorn City KY - gave the team a free dinner
Main Street Methodist Church, Tazewell - hosted the team the night before
planning_notes: Big A Mountain is about 6 miles and 1,500 ft of climbing, followed by steep descents with blind curves on narrow two-lane roads. Ride in a group and brake early.
A last-minute route change to avoid gravel led past a 'Private Property: No Trespassing' gate. Check the route on the ground before committing to it.
Dogs were roaming side roads around Breaks; plan a group-riding and yelling approach from here on.
Mi Rancho in Elkhorn City KY gave a free meal to the team.
Breaks Interstate Park campground has no electricity or water.

summary: Caroline was bitten by a loose dog on a back road leaving Breaks Interstate Park. The team waited hours for the rescue squad, sheriff and an ambulance, Caroline and Aarushi went to Pikeville Medical Center, and the whole team then SAG'd to Hazard KY.
slept_at: Bed and breakfast in Hazard KY (Harmony House, per the Day 15 post)
contacts: Charles, assistant director of the Challenger Learning Center, Hazard KY - host who drove a cargo van to shuttle the team
Haysi volunteer rescue team (VA) - responded to the bite
Pikeville Medical Center (KY) - gave Caroline the rabies shot series
planning_notes: The dog involved was a notorious dog that had bitten a cyclist before. Plan a dog protocol before the day starts, not during the incident.
Cell service dropped out on the rural road; walkie-talkies worked. Carry a backup communication device and save local emergency numbers.
Rural emergency response was slow: the rescue squad and sheriff took about an hour, and two counties (Dickenson and Buchanan) argued over jurisdiction.
Photograph the dog owner's license plate; the sheriff ran it and identified the owner.
The ambulance transfer to Pikeville took about 55 minutes including a wait for release, versus a 35-minute drive.
Six rabies shots were given in a circle around the wound at Pikeville Medical Center; ask the first responders about rabies and tetanus protocol.

summary: Taught at the Challenger Learning Center in Hazard KY to a talented group of kids. After the festival, the team had a planning meeting about whether to keep biking through dog country and decided to rent a pickup truck so any rider could be shuttled.
slept_at: Harmony House Bed & Breakfast, Hazard KY (per the Day 15 post)
learning_festival: Challenger Learning Center, Hazard KY: structured LF with advanced kids; older kids went into solenoids and motor spinning. The opener 'What is a magnet?' gauged each group's depth.
contacts: Charles, assistant director of the Challenger Learning Center, Hazard KY - coordinated the LF, lodging, meals and a 4-hour drive to help after the incident
planning_notes: Open the LF with 'What is a magnet?' to gauge grade level: youngest kids say it sticks to metal, older kids discuss polarity. Adjust depth on the fly.
A minivan holds 2 people (3 at most). To carry 5 riders and keep a SAG spot, rent a pickup or second vehicle.
Host Charles arranged dinner from Applebee's and the team had Dairy Queen blizzards after the festival.

summary: Rode 78.9 miles from Hazard to London KY with a follow car shadowing the riders and mace ready for dogs. A pickup reservation made online was not honored at the counter, and Tatiana sprained her ankle in the dark at the host's home.
slept_at: Lucy and Steve's home, London KY (backyard pool and gazebo)
contacts: Lucy and Steve, London KY - hosted; pool time, bolognese dinner, bonfire
planning_notes: Follow-car tactic: the car trails riders about 10 ft back at 10 mph with the horn and windows down, and uses walkie-talkies. It worked as a dog deterrent on this leg.
Mace was used on a pack of small dogs. A Great Dane chasing the riders hit a mailbox.
A pickup reserved online was not held: the rental counter had no pickup available. Call the counter to confirm the vehicle class before the day.
A rest stop with a splash pad and playground sits on this leg; it is a good break from dog zones.
A yard with about 20 large dogs in a cage on the route is a dog zone.

summary: Slept in a patched-together hammock setup at Lucy and Steve's in London KY, which was cold and poor for sleep. Rode 64.8 miles to Liberty KY through 6-8 dogs, and Tatiana needed three hospitals to get her sprain X-rayed.
slept_at: Liberty Assembly of God church, Liberty KY (host Brother Rodger)
contacts: Brother Rodger, Liberty Assembly of God - hosted; fried chicken and groceries
Lucy and Steve, London KY - hosted; breakfast spread
planning_notes: The two hammocks brought from home were missing parts. A 50-degree night in KY made hammock sleeping poor; bring a tent and check hammock parts before the trip.
The first hospital in a rural KY town had no X-ray machine; a sprain may require calling ahead for imaging.
Six to eight dogs chased riders on the last leg of this route, including a Rottweiler and a Great Pyrenees that ran between houses.
The Liberty laundromat closes early in the evening; do laundry earlier in the day.

summary: The injured driver drove the van while riders covered 88.8 miles from Liberty to a campground at Mammoth Cave KY. Stops included a waterfall at Brush Creek Baptist Church, a dinner at Farmwald's Dutch Bakery and Deli, and a donated dinner at La Cabana.
slept_at: Campground at Mammoth Cave, KY (name not given)
contacts: Pastor Roger Allen, Liberty KY - gave farm-fresh eggs; hosted at the fellowship hall
Mike and Nancy Tucker, Milby's Produce, KY - gave free cantaloupes
Louis and Nolasco, La Cabana Mexican Bar and Grill near Mammoth Cave - donated a dinner after one phone call
planning_notes: Farmwald's Dutch Bakery and Deli on the route is run by the local Amish community. It was a good emergency-fuel stop when riders were exhausted.
Brush Creek Baptist Church in KY has a river and waterfall on its grounds; a good rest stop.
The Mammoth Cave campground showers are coin-operated: 6 quarters for 4 minutes per person. Bring a lot of quarters.
The last 10 miles had 45 minutes of daylight left and a 2-mile climb to camp. Start the final stretch earlier.

summary: Returned the extra rental pickup early and lost camping items (two pillows, a sleeping pad, a camp chair, a hammock and a blanket) off the minivan's roof bag on I-65. The team toured Mammoth Cave, stopped at Buc-ee's, then biked 35.6 miles to Bowling Green, where Airbnbs were donated.
slept_at: Airbnb townhouses, Bowling Green KY (donated by Adam and Lindsey)
contacts: Adam and Lindsey, Bowling Green - donated two Airbnb townhouses
Sam, Bowling Green LF coordinator
Thai Thai, Bowling Green - free dinner for the team
Enterprise rental counter, Bowling Green - refunded $100 for returning the rental early
planning_notes: The roof storage bag had been falling off earlier in the trip (Luray and Elkhorn City). On I-65 it unzipped and lost camp gear. Check zippers and remove the bag before highway driving.
Mammoth Cave tours need booking; the team's 11:45 AM tour pushed the bike start to 3 PM.
Buc-ee's on the Mammoth Cave to Bowling Green stretch is a big food stop with brisket sandwiches and oversized drinks.
Bowling Green Airbnbs: two townhouses with 3 bedrooms each made a good rest-day base.

summary: Rest day in Bowling Green: Noah (Tatiana's boyfriend) arrived after a 10-hour drive. The team spent the day at Beech Bend waterpark and amusement park using a group season-pass discount.
slept_at: Airbnb, Bowling Green KY (Adam and Lindsey)
contacts: Adam and Lindsey, Bowling Green - Airbnb hosts
planning_notes: Beech Bend (Bowling Green KY) is a waterpark and amusement park in one. A season-pass group plan reduced the per-person price; lockers were $13.
Bring extra waterproof bandages: a dog-bite wound's bandage peeled off on a water slide.

summary: Taught the largest LF so far, about 100 kids in groups of 25 at the WKU Innovation Campus in Bowling Green. Afterward Howard's Bike Shop re-measured and realigned Aarushi's bike for free, and the team had a late-night downtown outing.
slept_at: Airbnb, Bowling Green KY
learning_festival: WKU Innovation Campus, Bowling Green KY: about 100 kids in groups of 25, grades 3 to high school. Older kids engaged deeply with genetic traits, which inspired a rework of the younger workshop.
contacts: Howard's Bike Shop, Bowling Green - re-measured and realigned Aarushi's bike for free
WKU Innovation Campus hosts and admin - ran the festival and posed for a team photo
planning_notes: WKU Innovation Campus can host about 100 kids; it ran as four groups of 25.
Howard's Bike Shop re-measured bike fit after a crash, at no charge.
Caroline's rabies series continued at a Bowling Green emergency room; a dose was given during this visit.

summary: Rode 87 miles from Bowling Green to a church in Madisonville KY. The team left about 90 minutes late after a late night, rode together for the first 24 miles, and napped at lunch. Sleeping bags and pads smelled badly from the roof storage.
slept_at: Life Christian Center church, Madisonville KY (Pastor Jon; slept in the church gym per the Day 22 post)
contacts: Pastor Jon, Life Christian Center, Madisonville KY - hosted; waited for the team
Morgan and Eddie - helped at a Fazoli's dinner stop
planning_notes: Sleeping bags, pads and pillows stored in the roof bag smelled like dirty socks by evening. Air gear out and dry it daily.
A late-night group (until 2 AM) delayed the next morning's start by 90 minutes. Set a group bedtime with a wakeup and departure plan.
A road closure on this route was passed through; check closures before the day and have an alternate.

summary: Rode 81.8 miles from Madisonville KY to Harrisburg IL in rain for the first 20 miles and before lunch. After crossing the Ohio River, the team cut a 7-mile detour that the 2025 route had added for an ice cream shop. Brad and Sherri hosted the team in Harrisburg.
slept_at: Brad and Sherri's home, Harrisburg IL (host)
contacts: Brad and Sherri, Harrisburg IL - hosted; fed chicken burritos
Pastor Jon and Life Christian Center, Madisonville KY - provided breakfast food and the church gym to sleep in
planning_notes: The 2025 route added 7 unnecessary miles to reach an ice cream shop. The 2026 team diverted south to skip it; compare old route files for detours before reusing them.
Carry your own rain jacket: one rider had to borrow one, and the team changed out of soaked jerseys at lunch.
Loose dogs in Kentucky remained the main hazard; the writer's review was 3 stars for the state.
Deer and armadillo carcasses on rural roads make for a hazardous, smelly approach; watch the shoulder.
